issue.title: New settings page listing upcoming booking reminders
issue.body:
Harness test (new screen). Add a new page under Settings where users see the reminder emails scheduled for their upcoming bookings (booking title, attendee, send time), read-only. Empty state when there are none.

Details from @lucasgrocha (comment 6756289657):
1. Compute the send time with a fixed rule: 24 hours before the booking start. No new scheduler or schema change.
2. Organizer only: bookings where the user is the host.

pm.summary: New read-only Settings page listing reminder emails for the host's upcoming bookings, send time fixed at 24h before start. This is a new screen, so it goes to the Designer next.
acceptance_criteria: A new page is reachable from the Settings navigation, with a clear title such as 'Booking reminders'.
The page lists one row per upcoming booking where the logged-in user is the organizer/host, showing booking title, attendee, and send time.
Send time equals the booking start time minus exactly 24 hours, shown in the user's timezone and locale format.
Bookings where the user is only an attendee are not listed.
Cancelled, rejected and past bookings are not listed.
Reminders whose computed send time is already in the past are still listed only if the booking is upcoming (decision: show them as is, no special state).
Rows are ordered by send time ascending.
When there are no matching bookings, an empty state with explanatory text is shown.
The page is read-only: no buttons or forms to edit, send or cancel reminders.
A logged-out user cannot access the page or its data; one user never sees another user's bookings.
No scheduler, database schema or migration changes are introduced.
All user-visible strings are in the English locale file.
Tests cover the 24h computation, host-only filtering and the empty state.

research.summary: Research done: settings pages are server page.tsx plus a client view, nav lives in SettingsLayoutAppDirClient. Data must be fetched without packages/trpc, which is out of scope. Next: PM decides, then the plan.
relevant_files: apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/settings/(settings-layout)/SettingsLayoutAppDirClient.tsx (nav items; my_account list with appearance/out_of_office entries around lines 62-75)
apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/settings/(settings-layout)/developer/webhooks/[id]/page.tsx (server page that reads data through a repository and prisma directly, no trpc)
packages/features/bookings/repositories/BookingRepository.ts (human-review area: read only; query shape with BookingStatus.ACCEPTED, userId, attendees)
packages/lib/dateTimeFormatter.ts (locale and timezone formatting helper) and packages/lib/dateTimeFormatter.test.ts (test style)
packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json (add strings such as booking_reminders, description, empty state, column labels)
patterns: New page = server page.tsx (generateMetadata via _generateMetadata, getServerSession check, redirect to /auth/login when logged out) rendering a client view from apps/web/modules/settings/my-account/*-view.tsx, imported as ~/settings/my-account/...
Nav entry: add an item with name (i18n key), href and trackingMetadata {section: "my_account", page: ...} to SettingsLayoutAppDirClient.tsx
Views wrap content in SettingsHeader (title, description, borderInShellHeader) and use useLocale() t(...) for every string

Constraint: packages/trpc is outside the allowed scope, so a trpc router is not an option. Fetch in the server page via a prisma query or a small helper in packages/features/ or packages/lib/, and pass props to the client view. Server-side session scoping gives the user isolation.

Avoid putting new files in the human-review prefixes packages/features/auth/, packages/lib/server/ and packages/features/bookings/lib/. Adding a method to BookingRepository.ts is also in the review area (bookings/repositories is not listed, but it is the natural place), so prefer a new file under packages/features/settings/ or a new feature folder.
Pure helper, e.g. computeReminderSendTime(start) = start minus 24h via dayjs or Date arithmetic, kept separate so it is unit-testable

Query filter: userId = session user (organizer only), status ACCEPTED (maybe also PENDING; PM said not cancelled or rejected), startTime > now, order by startTime asc. This implies send time ascending since the offset is constant. Select title, startTime, and attendees' name/email.
Format the send time with the user's timeZone and locale (dateTimeFormatter or Intl); get them from the user profile (timeZone, locale) or the session

Tests are colocated *.test.ts or *.test.tsx. Vitest workspace includes packages/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,js}, apps/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,js}, apps/web/modules/**/*.{test,spec}.tsx and packages/features/**/*.{test,spec}.tsx. Use .test.tsx for view/empty-state tests under apps/web/modules/ or packages/features/, and .test.ts for pure logic. Mock prisma for the host-only filter test.

design_need.summary: This is a new Settings screen, so design is needed. The Designer gets a brief for a read-only list of upcoming booking reminders with an empty state, then the plan follows.
design_need.design_brief:
Design a new read-only Settings page, "Booking reminders", reachable from the Settings navigation (My account group).

Purpose: a host sees which reminder emails are scheduled for their upcoming bookings. Send time is always 24 hours before the booking start.

Reuse the existing Settings patterns: the same header (title plus short description), the same list and empty-state styling as other settings pages (e.g. out of office), and the same navigation item style.

Content per row: booking title, attendee (name and email), send time (date and time in the user's timezone and locale). Rows are sorted by send time ascending. Only bookings where the user is the host are shown.

Please specify:
1. Page title and description copy.
2. List layout (table or stacked rows), column labels, and how it behaves on mobile (narrow width).
3. Handling of multiple attendees on one booking and of long titles or emails.
4. Empty state: icon, heading and explanatory text, with no call to action that edits anything.
5. Navigation label and position within Settings.
6. Loading is not a concern (server-rendered), but note any skeleton if you see fit.

Constraints: no buttons, forms or actions to edit, send or cancel reminders. Light and dark themes must work using existing UI components. All strings must be i18n-ready (English keys). Past-due send times for still-upcoming bookings are shown as normal rows, with no special state.

Deliver: a layout description or wireframe of the populated state and the empty state, the component list from the existing UI kit, and the final copy strings.
